channel.title: Gordon's Blog
channel.description: Essays on AI research, model scaling, agents, and markets by Gordon Guocheng Qian.

item.title: 从 SGD 到 Muon per head：优化器到底在控制什么？
item.description: 从 SGD、Adam、AdamW、LAMB 到 Muon、MuonClip：更新控制粒度如何从全局步长推进到每一个 attention head。

item.title: When 10,000-GPU Training Fails, How Does It Keep Going?
item.description: A visual map of stragglers, hard failures, slow recovery, and silent data corruption — with the response for each.

item.title: Transformer Parallelism
item.description: What data, tensor, pipeline, context, and expert parallelism actually partition.

item.title: Meta 什么都有了，唯独缺了文化
item.description: SemiAnalysis 复盘 Meta 超级智能一周年：数据、算力、人才、全球一半人口的用户，它全有了，唯独缺了最难补的那一样——文化。

item.title: 1 Gigawatt Is No Longer the Ceiling — It’s the Cover Charge
item.description: In 2024 no datacenter ran at a gigawatt. In 2026 five switch on, one per hyperscaler. A load sheet of who has how much power, how many chips, and how much Nvidia has actually sold — every number tagged by how far you can trust it.

item.title: A Visual Generation Practitioner’s Three Machines
item.description: A roaming laptop, a Mac mini running my agents around the clock, and an RTX 5090 that sleeps until something wakes it in 30 seconds.

item.title: One Git Repo to Sync All My Agents
item.description: Claude, Codex, and Hermes share one set of skills across three machines — and the only commands I run are git pull and git push.

item.title: 我的 Mac 连我的名字都记不住
item.description: 苹果自带的中文输入法不会记住你的常用字。Squirrel（Rime）记得住 —— 你的名字、常用词、甚至 emoji。配置也不用自己动手，交给你的 agent 就好。

item.title: I Build a Commentable Blog for Free with Claude in 20 Mins
item.description: A clean, free blog on GitHub Pages — likes, comments, email, and sharing to X, WeChat, Rednote, and Zhihu — built entirely by talking to an agent.

item.title: Priced In Is Not the Same as Exhausted
item.description: META's move reminded me why "it's already priced in" is often too lazy. Expectation, confirmation, and scale are different stages.

item.title: What Is the Next Scaling After Model Scaling?
item.description: Context scaling and agent scaling are the next product frontier — and both demand far more memory bandwidth. The HBM shortage is far from over.

item.title: Big Tech Research in Retreat: The Paper Era Is Ending
item.description: Research labs at the giants are shutting down, merging, and shrinking. This is the organizational reconstruction that follows AI industrialization.

item.title: How Gemini-Omni Might Work
item.description: Three plausible architectures for Google's latest video model, ranked — and why a Transfusion-style unified transformer is my top guess.

item.title: On-Policy Distillation: The Frontier Lab Recipe for Merging Experts
item.description: OPD is not just a loss function. It is how a thousand-person lab works in parallel on the same intelligence.

item.title: Post-training is demanding 10x pretraining's Computing
item.description: Two years ago pretraining used ~10x more compute than post-training. Six months ago the ratio was closer to 1:1. Now it may flip.

item.title: Visual Generation Models Are Becoming Chatbot Accessories
item.description: Visual generation is moving from standalone apps into chatbots, agents, and multimodal operating systems.

item.title: Agent Stock Skills: +20% in a Month, and Next Week's AI Watchlist
item.description: When an agent has million-token context and tracks policy, news, and market data faster than any retail investor, it becomes a real research edge.

item.title: Silicon Valley Has No Secrets. It Has Heretics.
item.description: Notes from Andrew Dai's interview: 14 years inside Google's AI machine, why he left after Gemini, and Elorian's bet on visual reasoning.

item.title: How I Use Hermes Agent as My Always-On Research and Writing Assistant
item.description: My setup for an 8am daily briefing, 10pm summaries, paper writing, blogging, and remote work from my phone.
